subject: Data handling clarifications and privacy addendum questions (post-demo)
messages:
From: Simon Jenkins <simon.jenkins@medlytics.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up from demo — quick data/questions

Laura — thanks for the walkthrough this morning. Team found the performance and routing discussion helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our legal/ops side before we move to procurement: 

1) Controller/Processor: we need a short paragraph that states when MedLytics is controller vs Redwood as processor for hosted inference. Can you confirm the language you typically include in the Privacy Addendum (PA)?
2) Subprocessors: can you provide the current list of subprocessors (cloud infra, monitoring, analytics) and confirm the notification process for adding new ones? Is there a 30/45/90 day notice?
3) Breach notification: what is Redwood's SLA for notifying customers of a confirmed data incident that affects customer data? Do you provide a timeline and sample playbook?
4) Logging & PII: what categories of PII will be present in logs/trace? Which fields are redacted by default and which are available for debugging under an NDA?
5) Data residency & retention: we need confirmation that data for our account can be pinned to us-east-1 and our retention policy is configurable (30/90/365 days).

Thx — attaching MedLytics legal checklist and an initial redline template. Can you or your legal ops contact respond with a short summary and proposed next steps (call + date)?

[Attachment: MedLytics_questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)]
[Attachment: MedLytics_privacy_redlines.docx (docx, 54KB)]

—Simon

Head of IT & Legal Ops
MedLytics

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Simon Jenkins <simon.jenkins@medlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — quick data/questions

Simon — thanks for the list and the redlines. Appreciate the detail. High-level answers below; Marissa is looped for legal ops specifics. If useful we can run a 30–45 minute legal ops call next week to go line-by-line. Proposed next step: we (Redwood) share a short PA summary + current subprocessor list and SOC2 artifacts, then schedule a call to walk the redlines.

1) Controller/Processor: Typical stance — MedLytics is Controller for customer-provided inputs and business decisions; Redwood is Processor for inference hosting and token-level processing. We include a paragraph in the PA that states this mapping and the responsibilities (data access, deletion requests, lawful basis). If you want alternate wording we can propose a customer-specific paragraph.

2) Subprocessors & notice: Current subprocessors: AWS (infrastructure), Redis Labs (caching), SegMetrics (usage analytics), Postmark (email). We provide a 30-day notice for material subprocessor additions; for critical infra changes we provide earlier communication. Formal list will be attached.

3) Breach notification: Redwood provides initial notification within 72 hours of confirming a security incident that materially affects customer data, followed by a remediation timeline and post-incident report. We can share our incident response playbook under NDA.

4) Logging & PII: By default we redact high-sensitivity fields from persistent logs (SSNs, full credit card numbers). Call traces may contain prompt/response snippets for debugging unless redaction is requested or a suppression policy is configured. We can enable stronger redaction and token scrubbing on dedicated/private deployments.

5) Data residency & retention: We support account-level residency (regions we operate in), and retention is configurable. Standard hosted retention options we support out-of-the-box: 30/90/365 days; custom longer retention can be arranged for Dedicated/Private.

Attachments I will share: Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW + pricing), current_subprocessors.csv, SOC2-summary.pdf.

Proposed next steps:
- I will email the PA summary + subprocessor list by EOD PST.
- Schedule legal ops call (Marissa to propose times).
- Redwood to review MedLytics redlines ahead of call.

Happy to set up a call — what times do you have Monday/Tuesday next week?

Best,

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187
[Attachment: Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf, 112KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — quick data/questions

Simon — looping in Redwood Legal/Ops here. Quick clarifying notes before the call: 

• Subprocessor cadence: we will share the exported list and the last updated timestamp. New subprocessor notices are emailed to the account contract contact; we can accept a preferred legal contact if you want that directed to "legal@medlytics.com".
• Incident notifications: 72 hours for confirmed incidents that meet the materiality threshold; if it's an account-only data leak we typically provide immediate customer-level notification once verified.
• Logs: we can provide filtered logs for debugging under an executed NDA/contract; full unredacted traces require explicit approval or a private deployment.
• Retention: confirm the retention window you want for the demo account (we can set the trial to 30 days by default).

I'll propose times for a 45-minute legal ops call. Please send any particularly sensitive examples you want to keep out of logs so we can include configuration notes in the runbook.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Legal Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
